name: Walt Disney
fiscalYearEnd: Saturday nearest September 30 (fiscal Q3 FY2026 ended June 27, 2026)
description: Disney has three segments. Experiences (theme parks and resorts, Disney Cruise Line, licensing and merchandise) earned $10.0B of the $17.6B segment operating profit in fiscal 2025, or 57 percent, at about a 30 percent margin. Entertainment (Disney+, Hulu, ABC and Disney channels, film studios and content licensing) earned $4.7B, with the streaming business now profitable and a shrinking linear TV business still contributing $3.0B. Sports (ESPN and its streaming service, launched August 2025) earned $2.9B. Cash flows fund about $9B of capital spending, dividends and a buyback of at least $9B in fiscal 2026. Recent deals: control of Fubo (70 percent, October 2025), ESPN taking NFL Network and media assets (January 2026), and a sale of half of A+E Networks to a Hearst affiliate for about $1.2B (July 2026).

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge; not checked against an MSCI/S&P source. In practice about 57 percent of segment operating profit in FY2025 came from theme parks, cruises and consumer products, which the Movies & Entertainment box does not suggest.

hq.note: From general knowledge; not re-read from the 10-K cover.

businessLines.name: Experiences
businessLines.how: Guests pay for park tickets, hotel stays, food, merchandise and cruises; profit rises with attendance, hotel and cruise capacity, and per-guest spending. Consumer products earns licence royalties and sells merchandise.

revenue.note: Q3 FY2026 $10.0B (+10%); FY2025 revenue by segment was not extracted

businessLines.revenueNote: Q3 FY2026 $10.0B (+10%); FY2025 revenue by segment was not extracted

operatingProfit.note: Nine months FY2026 $8.94B (+10%), about a 30% margin (computed 8.94 / 29.5); Q3 FY2026 $3.02B (+20%). Revenue share is of the sum of segment revenues for the nine months (segment revenues sum to $78.2B against $76.4B consolidated, difference is intersegment eliminations).

businessLines.name: Entertainment
businessLines.how: Streaming: monthly subscription fees plus advertising on Disney+, Hulu and Hotstar. Linear TV: fees paid by cable and satellite distributors per subscriber plus advertising. Studios: theatrical box office, licensing and home entertainment sales.

revenue.note: Q3 FY2026 $11.3B (+6%), of which subscription and affiliate fees $7.55B (+12%), advertising $1.63B (-1%), content sales $1.60B (-6%)

businessLines.revenueNote: Q3 FY2026 $11.3B (+6%), of which subscription and affiliate fees $7.55B (+12%), advertising $1.63B (-1%), content sales $1.60B (-6%)

operatingProfit.note: FY2025: Linear Networks $2,960M, Direct-to-Consumer $1,330M, Content Sales/Licensing $392M. Nine months FY2026 $4.12B (+3%); Q3 FY2026 $1.68B (+64%)

businessLines.name: Sports
businessLines.how: ESPN earns affiliate fees from cable and streaming distributors and advertising on live sports, and pays large multi-year rights fees to leagues; ESPN's direct-to-consumer service launched August 2025 adds subscription revenue.

operatingProfit.note: Nine months FY2026 $1.70B (-14%); Q3 FY2026 $858M (-17%), due to higher programming and production costs including the NBA renewal timing and new sports rights

brands.name: Disney+, Hulu, Hotstar (SVOD)
brands.share: Q3 FY2026 revenue $5.53B, about 49% of Entertainment revenue (computed)

brands.name: ESPN
brands.share: Sports segment, $14.0B nine-month revenue; Disney's effective interest in the ESPN and NFL Network combination is 72% (Hearst 18%)

brands.name: Fubo (with Hulu Live TV)
brands.share: Disney holds 70 percent on a fully diluted basis (October 2025)

brands.name: A+E Networks
brands.share: Agreed July 2026 to sell a 50% stake to a Hearst affiliate for about $1.2B
